---
title: "Canton flag labels"
description: "Create Datawrapper-compatible canton labels in R."
---

<div class="toolbox-kind">Snippet</div>

```r
library(stringr)

canton_with_flag <- function(canton, base_url) {
  stopifnot(nzchar(base_url))
  base_url <- str_remove(base_url, "/$")

  as.character(
    str_glue(
      "![{canton}]({base_url}/{canton}.svg) {canton}"
    )
  )
}

flag_base_url <- "https://assets.example.org/canton-flags"
canton_with_flag("AG", flag_base_url)
#> ![AG](https://assets.example.org/canton-flags/AG.svg) AG
```

This produces Markdown-style labels for Datawrapper. Replace the example base URL with a stable, publicly approved asset host. Do not publish an internal or organization-specific asset URL in this repository.

## Canton metadata

Keep `tamMap::canton_CH()` as the organization-specific source of truth rather than duplicating a canton table.

```r
cantons <- tamMap::canton_CH() |>
  dplyr::select(
    iso2,
    iso4,
    french1,
    german1,
    ita,
    eng,
    order,
    lang,
    lon,
    lat
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(cantons) == 26,
  !anyDuplicated(cantons$iso2)
)
```

The package was checked on 2026-10-04: `canton_CH()` returned 26 rows and 23 fields. `iso2` contains the two-letter canton code used by the flag helper; `iso4` contains values such as `CH-AG`.
